{
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "incident_category", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.95, "rationale": "Categorizing incidents (email, vpn, database) gives a genuine axis to compare resolution times across ticket types. Values are sound readings of short_description (e.g. 'Unable to access the database' -> database)."},
    {"name": "incident_symptom_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Symptom type (connection_failure, outage, access_denied) is a useful axis for resolution difficulty. Mostly grounded, though 'Unable to access the database' -> access_denied is a mild inference and 'Software update issue' -> other is defensible."},
    {"name": "scope_indicator", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Scope (individual vs server-wide) is a strong predictor of resolution time. However short descriptions rarely state scope explicitly; defaulting most rows to 'individual_user' is a plausible but partly unwarranted inference where the text is silent."},
    {"name": "problem_specificity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.5, "source_groundedness": 0.55, "rationale": "Somewhat overlaps with incident_symptom_type. 'generic_connectivity' assigned even to 'Unable to access the database' and 'Software update issue' (non-connectivity) shows the label is loosely grounded and near-default."},
    {"name": "remote_access_context", "analytical_usefulness": 0.65, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Flags remote/VPN context, plausibly relevant to resolution effort. VPN row -> True is well grounded; other rows defaulting to False is a reasonable reading."},
    {"name": "assigned_agent", "analytical_usefulness": 0.95, "source_groundedness": 0.8, "rationale": "Directly central to a query about per-agent resolution times. Appears to restate/normalize the existing assigned_to column, but agent identity is grounded and essential for this analysis."},
    {"name": "reassignment_indicator", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.35, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "Reassignment is a strong signal for longer resolution, but the source columns shown do not support determining reassignment; assigning True/False per row appears largely invented/unwarranted from the available text."},
    {"name": "ticket_open_status", "analytical_usefulness": 0.4, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "Derivable from state/closed_at, but near-constant (478 false vs 22 true) and largely redundant with existing 'state', limiting analytical leverage."},
    {"name": "opened_day_of_week", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.95, "rationale": "Directly derived from opened_at; a legitimate temporal axis that could correlate with resolution delays (weekend openings)."},
    {"name": "opened_hour_of_day", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "Business vs after-hours bucketing of opened_at is a plausible driver of slower resolution and is grounded in the timestamp."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.72,
  "source_groundedness": 0.75,
  "hallucination_observed": true,
  "rationale": "Most added columns provide genuine new axes (category, symptom, agent, temporal buckets, remote context) directly relevant to modeling what drives longer resolution times, and are largely well grounded in short_description and timestamps. Weaknesses: reassignment_indicator appears fabricated with no supporting source column; problem_specificity is loosely grounded and overlaps with symptom_type; ticket_open_status is near-constant and redundant with state; scope_indicator over-relies on a default 'individual_user' inference. Overall a useful and mostly grounded augmentation with a couple of ungrounded or low-leverage columns."
}
